Title: May 7, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Regular Meeting
Overview: The May 7, 2026 Boulder City Council regular meeting opened with extended public comment on proposed tipped minimum wage changes, a residential vacancy tax, and FAA airport grants, and included a Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons declaration. Council approved the consent agenda, unanimously adopted Ordinance 8741 to landmark 745 University Avenue as the Polls and Registration House, and reviewed call-up items including the Presbyterian Manor concept plan. Council adopted Ordinance 8745, the Omnibus land use code amendment, on second reading by a 5 to 1 vote, with an added amendment removing outdoor patio size limits for breweries and related venues.

Topic1.Title: Call to Order, Roll Call and Removal of Item 4E
Topic1.Summary: Mayor Brockett called the meeting to order and the council confirmed a quorum. Council unanimously voted to remove item 4E from the consent agenda, which kept the June 11 study session as scheduled rather than canceling it for an in-person special meeting.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment Period
Topic2.Summary: Residents spoke for two minutes each, with many opposing cuts to the tipped minimum wage and citing the city's living wage figures. Speakers urged the council to place a residential vacancy tax on the ballot at $5,000 per unit, opposed FAA grants that would commit the airport in perpetuity, and raised concerns about land use rules affecting a lot split. Other speakers addressed South Boulder Rec Center pool closure concerns, a Bike Boulder bike registration drive, and the Israel and Gaza divestment issue. Staff said a tip credit discussion will return later in the year, and council said a July public hearing on tip offsets was planned. Council members used their closing remarks to thank speakers and respond to comments.

Topic3.Title: National Day of Awareness for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons Declaration
Topic3.Summary: Council Member Adams presented a declaration recognizing the National Day of Awareness for Missing and Murdered Indigenous Persons, and the mayor signed it. The declaration calls on city departments to recognize root causes and calls on Boulder law enforcement to receive Colorado-specific training. Speakers from Harvest of All First Nations and community connectors asked for real action beyond proclamations, including reparations, land access, and accountability. A speaker also warned that surveillance tools like license plate readers could increase criminalization of Indigenous communities. Council thanked the speakers and committed to continued efforts to keep residents safe and heard.

Topic4.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic4.Summary: Council considered the consent agenda, which included items 4A through 4D and 4F through 4L, with item 4E previously removed. A council member asked about the beverage licensing authority rules amendment, and staff confirmed a public hearing would occur on second reading. Council then approved the consent agenda unanimously by roll call.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins and Presbyterian Manor Concept Plan
Topic5.Summary: Council reviewed call-up items 5A through 5F, including landmark alteration applications for 409 Mountain View Road and relocation of two buildings at 2106 Arapahoe Avenue. Item 5D was a height modification at 1039 Mapleton Avenue, and item 5E was an outside city utility permit at 1420 Cherryvale Road. For item 5F, the concept plan for permanently affordable senior housing at Presbyterian Manor, staff explained that potential code changes on demolition timing would not apply to this application. Council members raised questions on timing and tax credits, but no items were called up for further review.

Topic6.Title: Landmark Designation of 745 University Avenue (Ordinance 8741)
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented a request to designate the 1907 house at 745 University Avenue as an individual landmark, to be named the Polls and Registration House. The house served as a polling place for two decades, hosted caucuses and World War I registration, and was the site of 1917 municipal elections that created the city charter and proportional voting. The owners, Celeste Landry and Eric Cornell, spoke about the house's voting history, and Historic Boulder supported the designation. Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8741 by roll call, making it the city's 222nd individual landmark.

Topic7.Title: Omnibus Land Use Code Amendment (Ordinance 8745)
Topic7.Summary: Staff presented the Omnibus code amendment, a cleanup ordinance that removes office floor area limits, clarifies ADU utilities, allows driveways to remain after garage conversions, and allows height modifications up to 55 feet for three-story community, cultural, or educational uses. Council added an amendment removing outdoor patio size limits for breweries, tap rooms, and tasting rooms, which the staff confirmed could return on third reading. Council members raised concerns about the height change and the breadth of eligible uses, and asked staff to narrow the list. Council voted 5 to 1 to amend and pass Ordinance 8745 on second reading, with third reading expected at the next business meeting.
